text: Count data arise frequently applied statistics: number physician office visits, number articles published, number insurance claims. simplest model count data Poisson regression, assumes mean equals variance. practice, two violations common: Overdispersion. variance often exceeds mean. negative binomial (NB) model addresses introducing dispersion parameter θ>0\theta > 0 Var(Yi)=μi+μi2/θ\text{Var}(Y_i) = \mu_i + \mu_i^2/\theta. θ→∞\theta \\infty model reduces Poisson. Excess zeros. Many count datasets contain zeros Poisson (even NB) distribution predicts. zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model (Lambert 1992) handles two-component mixture: probability πi\pi_i observation structural zero (e.g., person never visits doctor); probability 1−πi1-\pi_i comes NB distribution, can produce zeros. report documents nbzinbAmoah R package, fits models scratch using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) (McCullagh Nelder 1989) expectation-maximisation (EM) algorithm — without general-purpose optimizer. benchmark implementation reference functions MASS::glm.nb() (Venables Ripley 2002) pscl::zeroinfl() (Zeileis et al. 2008), apply package NMES1988 dataset AER package (Kleiber Zeileis 2008).

nbzinbAmoah package exports four user-facing functions: fitting functions return S3 objects (classes "nbreg" "zinbreg") containing coefficients, variance–covariance matrix, θ̂\hat\theta standard error, log-likelihood, number iterations, convergence flag, fitted values matched call. Methods provided print, summary (coefficient table estimates, SEs, zz values pp-values, printed print.summary method), coef, vcov, logLik (df attribute, AIC() BIC() work), fitted, residuals (type = "response" "pearson"), nobs, predict (newdata). zinbreg, coef() vcov() take model = "count", "zero" "full", predict() supports type = "response" ((1−π)μ(1-\pi)\mu), "count" (μ\mu) "zero" (π\pi). zinbreg formula uses two-part syntax y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2 Formula package: count-model covariates bar zero-model covariates . Without |, covariates used parts, zeroinfl().

project implemented NB ZINB regression scratch, using IRLS Newton–Raphson (NB) EM algorithm IRLS M-steps (ZINB). general-purpose optimizer used fitting code. benchmarking results confirm implementation reproduces MASS::glm.nb() within 3.72e-10 pscl::zeroinfl() within 1.51e-05 coefficients, log-likelihood differences 9.97e-10. well within required tolerances (10−510^{-5} NB 10−310^{-3} ZINB coefficients). simulation study (RR = 100, nn = 500) shows zinbreg() reliably recovers known ZINB parameters negligible bias well-calibrated 95% Wald intervals (empirical coverage 0.93–0.95). Limitations. First, NB standard errors β\beta treat θ\theta known, glm.nb() , ignore uncertainty θ̂\hat\theta. Second, ZINB standard errors use numerical Hessian, slower can less accurate analytic one. Third, EM converges linearly, zinbreg() needs many iterations several times slower zeroinfl() (see timing table). Fourth, offsets supported count model , zero model. Finally, NMES1988 analysis zero-model covariates follow project description, choice NB ZINB relies information criteria rather formal test, usual likelihood-ratio test non-standard null value πi=0\pi_i = 0 lies boundary parameter space. Possible extensions include analytic Hessian ZINB standard errors, offset zero model, acceleration EM algorithm (example, switching Newton–Raphson near convergence), formal score test zero inflation.

title: Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression — zinbreg
text: formula two-part formula y ~ count_covariates | zero_covariates. | omitted, covariates used parts. data data frame. offset optional offset count part (log scale). control list zinbreg_control. weights Optional prior weights.

title: Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression — zinbreg
text: object class "zinbreg" components: coefficients List count (beta) zero (gamma). theta Estimated dispersion parameter. loglik Observed-data log-likelihood convergence. vcov Variance-covariance matrix (numerical Hessian observed loglik). fitted.values Expected counts \((1-\pi_i)\mu_i\). fitted.pi Estimated zero-inflation probabilities \(\pi_i\). fitted.mu Estimated NB means \(\mu_i\). residuals Response residuals \(y - (1-\pi)\mu\). nobs Number observations. df.residual Residual degrees freedom. iter Number EM iterations. converged Logical. call matched call.

title: Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression — zinbreg
text: model two components: Count part: \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\) Zero part: \(\text{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top \gamma\) Specify parts two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2. | present, covariates used parts.
